purpose: Watermark for stopping-review cycles. A review processes EVERY route whose counter is > last_reviewed_route_counter, regardless of when or by which agent its logs were synced locally. Do NOT anchor a review on 'whatever was just downloaded' -- another agent may sync routes for unrelated reasons, and the routes you need may already be local or only on the device. After completing a review, set last_reviewed_route_counter to the highest route processed and append a review_log entry. Routes <= the cursor are considered done and are not re-reviewed.
procedure: 2. Enumerate routes on BOTH the device (/data/media/0/realdata) and locally (~/.route_sync/data/media/0/realdata) with counter > cursor.
3. Sync any missing ones logs-only (tools/route_sync/refresh_routes.py --include-rlog; never video).
4. Analyze the union; for V2 stopping reviews, key on engaged longControlState==stopping runs (not just v<0.1, which catches manual/disengaged stops).
5. Update last_reviewed_route_counter to the highest counter processed; append a review_log entry; commit.

review_log.finding: Bookmark review: the cruise fault RECURRED (user: 'that part didn't work') after the prior StopReq-on-override fix (c06b9ea4db). Root cause re-diagnosed and PROVEN: longitudinal_planner.py:899 forced output_should_stop=True for force-coast+standstill -> holds via the SCC managed stop (StopReq) -> with NO lead the car's TCS treats it as invalid and disables ACC (accFaulted) the instant the driver gas-overrides. Corpus proof: 25 gas-resume-from-stop events -> 2/2 no-lead force-coast resumes FAULTED, 0/23 lead-backed resumes clean. distanceToStopTarget=-1 at both faults (should_stop was force-coast-forced, not MPC). The prior frame-fix could not help: the fault is the car reacting to BEING in a no-lead managed stop (override at t=51.5 -> ACC disabled -> accFaulted t=52.3, StopReq already 0). FIX (db889cd638, deployed): apply_force_coast_standstill_hold() only forces the managed stop when an actionable lead (<8m) backs it; no-lead -> hold via firm openpilot brake (-1.0, no should_stop -> no StopReq) so the resume is a plain override the SCC accepts. Also lifts force-coast's firm braking off the gentle no-lead stop (user's 2nd point: 'could be smoother, no lead'). 4 new CI regression tests; logic verified standalone + ruff/compile. User accepted on-road verification of hold firmness (firm-hold IS the StopReq we removed). 0000175a: NO engaged stops (0 stopping frames), force-coast only at highway speed (segs6-7, 18-37 m/s coast), 0 accFaulted -> clean, nothing to tune.
